What this adapter does

Read Shopify Orders and transaction-history CSVs locally, combine multi-line orders correctly, reconcile split captures, and run MerchantOps’ tested financial models. No store credentials are needed. Real exports must match the supported profile and include the required supplementary records.

The supported profile is deliberately narrow

Paid, unrefunded INR orders; SKUs unique within each order; successful sale/capture transactions. Taxes, shipping charged to customers, discounts, refunds, cancelled orders, ambiguous transaction rows and missing costs are rejected. Nothing unsupported is silently dropped. This is not a live Shopify app.

Why a CSV alone is not enough

Historical item cost, actual fulfilment expense, payment fees, stable customer keys and provider transaction IDs must come from your records. The preparation command creates a local template to fill. MerchantOps never invents zero costs or treats an order’s payment-reference list as proof of collected cash.

A small example you can check by hand

Two tees at ₹50 plus one bag at ₹30. Two captures: ₹80 and ₹50. Subtract ₹40 item cost, ₹5 fulfilment and ₹2.60 fees: ₹82.40 contribution before advertising. The example uses synthetic Shopify-shaped files, not a real merchant export.

Run it locally

python -m merchantops.shopify run \
  --orders examples/shopify/orders.csv \
  --transactions examples/shopify/transactions.csv \
  --context examples/shopify/context.json \
  --database shopify-demo.duckdb \
  --as-of 2026-06-30 --report-dir store-reports

Replay the same input: zero new records. Dates use your declared store timezone. Source totals and captures must match exactly. Changed previously imported order lines or costs are rejected. Keep real exports and reports local; the public build uses only checked-in synthetic examples.

What has not been verified

No real merchant export, Shopify development store or live API has been tested. Compatibility is checked against synthetic fixtures shaped from Shopify’s documented CSV headers. The 100,000-order benchmark elsewhere measures the canonical pipeline, not this adapter. Advertising is absent from these exports; acquisition performance is not established.
